bib.title: A Decomposable Attention Model for Natural Language Inference

question: Can natural language inference be solved by aligning local text pieces with attention and aggregating, without deep sentence encoders?
hypothesis: For NLI it can often suffice to simply align bits of local text substructure and then aggregate this information.
contributions: A simple attend-compare-aggregate NLI model that is trivially parallelizable
State-of-the-art SNLI accuracy with almost an order of magnitude fewer parameters, without word-order information
Optional intra-sentence attention with distance-sensitive bias gives further gains

method.summary: Embeddings of premise and hypothesis are soft-aligned with a feed-forward attention (Attend), each word is compared with its aligned phrase by a feed-forward net G (Compare), and the summed comparison vectors go to a classifier H (Aggregate). Optional intra-sentence attention adds minimal order information.

datasets.name: SNLI
datasets.size: 549,367 train / 9,842 dev / 9,824 test pairs after removing '-' labels (570K total)
datasets.preprocessing: tokenized sentences from non-binary parse; NULL token prepended; batch padding masked; semi-sorted by length (<20, <50, rest)

other.embedding_norm: l2 norm 1, then projection to 200 dims (tuned)

models.name: Decomposable Attention + intra-sentence attention
models.architecture: as vanilla with self-attention and distance bias terms, distances over 10 bucketed together

training.optimizer: Adagrad, initial accumulator value 0.1, 10 asynchronous gradient-update threads on a single machine
training.batch_size: 4 (footnote: 16 or 32 also work well and are a bit more stable)
training.steps: 50 million steps (each step one batch); best dev checkpoint kept
training.dropout: 0.2 on all ReLU layers, not final linear layer

metrics.name: 3-class accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of correctly classified SNLI pairs

eval.protocol: single run, checkpoint chosen on dev set, test accuracy reported; no seeds or significance tests stated

evidence.where: 5.1; footnote 1 reads '16 or 32 also work well and are a bit more stable'

results.claim: Intra-sentence attention variant reaches 86.8% SNLI test accuracy, 0.5 points over previous state of the art.
results.setup: SNLI test set, 3-class accuracy, single model, 582K params
results.table: Table 1, row Our approach with intra-sentence attention, column Test Acc

results.claim: Vanilla model matches the best prior test accuracy with 382K parameters versus 3.4M for LSTMN.
results.setup: SNLI test set, 3-class accuracy, single model, 382K params, no word order
results.table: Table 1, row Our approach (vanilla), column Test Acc

results.claim: Vanilla model has 382K parameters excluding embeddings.
Dev-set gains come mostly from neutral, losses from contradiction.
results.quote: most of our gains stem from neutral, while most losses come from contradiction pairs
results.table: Table 2, row Our approach w/ intra att., column N

limits: Only SNLI evaluated; no other NLI datasets
Cannot use word order: fails on examples needing sequence information or numbers (Table 3 F, H, I)
Embeddings not fine-grained enough for some contradictions (play/watch)
Complexity analysis assumes sentence length < embedding dim
Single runs, no seeds or variance reported

lineage.work: Rocktäschel et al. LSTM with attention

figures.caption: Pictoral overview of the approach, showing the Attend (left), Compare (center) and Aggregate (right) steps.
figures.why: Shows the three-step decomposition at a glance.
